llm.summary: The skill can perform TikTok product lookups, but it also adds account, billing, automatic feedback sharing, and broad local persistence behaviors that need review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Credential-bearing requests use environment-overridable base URLs without host allowlisting, and the product scripts forward session/message/mode/app metadata along with the API key.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer was found, but onboarding guidance asks users to install unpinned Python packages when needed and to persist the LinkFox API key in shell profile or system environment settings.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger includes broad product-analytics language, and the feedback instruction tells the agent to report praise, dissatisfaction, mismatches, or anything improvable to an external API without interrupting the user's flow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The scripts always write full responses and cache files locally, may fall back to home or temp directories despite documentation saying not to use /tmp, and use unsanitized SESSION_ID values in output paths.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ranking and product-detail scripts match the stated Kalodata/TikTok purpose, but the package also ships SMS login, API-key generation, account/team inspection, subscription listing, order creation, payment QR rendering, and feedback submission.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you are comfortable with LinkFox account, billing, and feedback workflows living inside a product lookup skill. Use a dedicated API key, verify LINKFOX_* endpoint environment variables are not overridden, avoid sharing phone verification codes through the agent unless necessary, confirm any paid order manually, and delete local linkfox output/cache files when they are no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Confirmed that product and onboarding scripts send credentials to base URLs that can be changed by environment variables; network API calls are expected, but arbitrary credential-bearing destinations are not.
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed that the skill includes account, subscription, order, and payment QR workflows beyond read-only product analytics; these are disclosed as auth/billing remediation but materially expand scope.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The activation text is mostly TikTok-product focused but includes generic product-analytics wording that could trigger the skill more broadly than a user intended.
[P6] expected: The referenced Display Rules are ordinary result-formatting instructions; I did not find artifact evidence of system-prompt extraction.
[YR1] expected: The matched shell-profile command persists an API key for setup; it is not a backdoor payload, but users should understand it creates a long-lived credential.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed scope expansion into login, account, package, order, and payment actions that are not core product ranking/detail retrieval.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifacts do not define tight permission boundaries despite using external network calls, local writes, credentials, and billing-related actions.
[SQP-2] expected: Local response persistence is disclosed and supports large API results, but it is mandatory, stores full responses, and lacks clear opt-in or retention controls.
[SSD-3] expected: Full-response storage is part of the documented workflow, but it can retain commercially sensitive product research and session-linked metadata.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed two separate concerns: phone/OTP handling in onboarding and automatic feedback submission containing user statements or inferred intent.
[E1] expected: The curl examples send product requests to the documented LinkFox gateway, which is expected for an external data API skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed documentation says output should stay under the current working directory and not use /tmp, while scripts can fall back to home and temp locations.
[T01] unexpected: Confirmed the SARIF concern: feedback reporting is an unrelated outbound objective and is instructed to occur without interrupting the user for explicit approval.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed credential-bearing environment-controlled destinations, extra agent metadata headers, and unsanitized SESSION_ID path construction.
[T08] expected: No malicious dependency is embedded, but unpinned pip install guidance appears in a flow that can handle authentication and payment-related data.
